$comment: Conditional reporting policies per result type (hep-authoring plan T5). A policy checks the method metadata a record supplies; it never chooses the method or invents a default. `when` conditions compare dotted keys of reporting_context.method (equality, or {"not": value}); `when_absent` says what an absent key means: unknown (default: the field's applicability is unresolved), applicable, or not-applicable. `conflicts_with` marks a field that must not be provided under that method (error reporting.interval_kind_mismatch). Field states in a record: provided, missing, not-applicable (needs a reason), unresolved. Version 1.1.0 (RC-C3) adds flux-measurement; 1.2.0 (Com2) adds five flux-measurement fields, each required only when the method declares it, so records that do not declare those methods keep their results. Comparison and interpretation claims get no policy of their own: their completeness is that of the results they compare or interpret (each with its own reporting_context), and their wording rules are in references/scientific-style.md.

measurement.description: a measured quantity with its uncertainties

unit.description: the unit of the value ('1' for dimensionless)

uncertainty_definition.description: what the quoted uncertainty is (68% interval, standard deviation, ...)

systematic_uncertainty.description: the systematic component; not-applicable with a reason when none is quoted

scope.description: the sample, phase space and conditions the value holds for

corrections_applied.description: which corrections (efficiency, acceptance, exposure, unfolding) the value includes

search.description: a significance statement about a signal hypothesis

trials_method.description: how the look-elsewhere correction was obtained

expected_significance.description: the expected (median) significance under the signal hypothesis

observed_vs_expected.description: a statement that observed and expected are distinguished wherever quoted

scope.description: the hypothesis, mass or parameter range and dataset the statement holds for

limit.description: an upper or lower limit, frequentist or Bayesian

construction.description: the interval construction (CLs, Feldman-Cousins, profile likelihood, ...)

prior.description: the prior on the parameter of interest (Bayesian)

expected_construction.description: how the expected limit was obtained (Asimov, toys, ...); an expected limit does not by itself imply Asimov data

scope.description: the model, parameter range and dataset the limit holds for

scale_choice.description: the renormalization and factorization scale choice

scale_uncertainty.description: how the theory uncertainty was estimated (scale envelope, ...)

pdf_set.description: the PDF set and its uncertainty treatment

validity_domain.description: the kinematic or parameter domain the prediction is valid in

ml-result.description: a machine-learning performance or inference result

metric_definition.description: the metric and how it is computed

evaluation_split.description: the evaluation split and its grouping (leakage control)

seed_variance.description: the variance over seeds or retrainings

baseline.description: the baseline compared against, with matched budget

training_domain.description: the domain the model was trained on (extrapolation control)

flux-measurement.description: a differential flux (spectrum) per rigidity or energy bin, as measured by a cosmic-ray or astroparticle instrument

quantity_and_unit.description: what is binned (rigidity, kinetic energy per nucleon, total energy) and the flux unit, e.g. m^-2 sr^-1 s^-1 GV^-1

binning.description: the bin edges and where each point sits in its bin (e.g. Lafferty-Wyatt for an assumed spectral shape)

exposure.description: how the exposure was formed (acceptance times live time), each entering once

acceptance.description: the acceptance and its corrections (simulation, data-driven efficiency corrections)

live_time.description: the live time per bin, with the geomagnetic-cutoff treatment for an instrument in orbit

unfolding.description: how the rigidity or energy resolution was unfolded (method, regularisation)

scale_systematic.description: the rigidity- or energy-scale uncertainty and how it propagates to the flux

period.description: the data-taking period, which fixes the solar-modulation conditions

refold_kit.description: what lets a reader fold their own model through the result: the response (or per-era responses), the exposure per bin and their conventions

collection_time_definition.description: how the collection time per bin was formed (live time above the cutoff, safety factor, quality cuts), as in collection_time.py

bin_position.description: where each point sits in its bin and why (Lafferty-Wyatt for a stated spectral shape, or another stated rule)

variable_conversion.description: how the flux was converted to another variable (Jacobian and bin averaging, isotope composition), as in spectrum_transform.py

era.description: the detector configurations (eras) the result spans, and how era differences enter the uncertainties
